sheep.text: It chews, looks up, and regards you with deep sheep wisdom, which on closer inspection is a blank. A good blank. Very well maintained.

wall_mender.text: Mind your elbows, I'm mending the wall. A drystone wall is held up by weight and gravity and nothing else. Same as me.
The Mourne Wall took 18 years and about 200 men to build. They'd stop for the weather, I'm told, and then get on with the weather anyway.

shepherd.text: The sheep up here know where every gap in the wall is. We have a gentleman's agreement: they stay in, and I don't ask how.
A lamb's got more sense than a dog on a bad day. Don't tell the dog.

peat_cutter.text: Well now! Nobody comes in here without wading. Have a sit. The kettle's on, and so, I'm told, is the fog.
My granda cut peat on this very bog for the fire. These days we leave it wet to keep the carbon in. Same peat, newer manners.

mourne_rambler.text: I'm walking the whole of the Wall in a day. I'm on hour six. I'm on tile number... Look, there's a lot of wall.
The trick is snacks. Soda farl, a flask, and a heart full of denial.
